title: Solutions to the Einstein-scalar-field system in spherical symmetry with large bounded variation norms
relevance: Direct source audit for Theorem 1.7, smooth compact incoming profiles, finite-cone uniform estimates, Proposition 3.18 in §3.8, and the u0→−∞ compactness passage in §4.
limits: Selective full-text audit of the theorem, displayed estimates, axis setup, and limiting argument; not a line-by-line reproof. Establishes quotient-level estimates and convergence stated in the paper; does not state C2/C∞ metric regularity in an axis-regular four-dimensional atlas or C1 dependence of the scattering limit on the profile.
assumptions: Spherical Einstein–massless-scalar system with Ric=2 dφ⊗dφ; smooth profile Φ satisfying (1.20), sufficiently small amplitude/integral bounds for fixed γ; bounded Φ'' for Proposition 3.18.
conclusion: Constructs a two-sided causally geodesically complete scattering solution. Proposition 3.18 gives finite higher-order quotient estimates uniform in the initial cone parameter. Section 4 extracts a limit with (φ, ∂v(rφ), ∂u(rφ)) converging in C1, r in C2, and m in C1 on compact quotient sets.
proof_status: Theorem and estimates proved in source; regular-chart metric-axis upgrade and profile differentiability are not asserted there.
dependencies: Theorem 1.7 uses Theorem 1.1 and Proposition 3.18; characteristic local existence/uniqueness and the reduced Einstein–scalar equations in §§2–4.
open_questions: Do uniform estimates for the reconstructed regular-chart metric through second order, including m/r and axis compatibility, hold as u0→−∞?
Can the finite-cone solution map and its linearization be controlled uniformly in u0 and passed to a unique or canonically selected scattering limit?

title: Global non-linearly stable large-data solutions to the Einstein scalar field system
relevance: Direct follow-up method audit for all-order estimates and regularity at the spherical axis; tests whether the LOY scattering-limit gap was already closed in a related paper.
limits: The paper explicitly does not directly control the global past-null-infinity scattering solutions of Luk–Oh–Yang. Its all-order estimates are for solutions to the future of a cone and a later Cauchy extension, so they do not establish uniform-in-u0 axis-inclusive estimates for the LOY scattering limit or C1 profile dependence.

locators.scope: §1, especially stated cone-based method and limitation on past-null-infinity solutions

assumptions: Spherically symmetric Einstein–scalar solutions generated from sufficiently regular characteristic cone data, with the decay and geometric hypotheses of Theorem 3.1; later stability results require further regularity.
conclusion: Derives higher-order estimates for a cone-based class, addressing terms near the axis, and discusses regularity of reconstructed spacetime quantities; explicitly leaves direct control of LOY's two-sided past-null-infinity scattering solutions outside scope.
proof_status: Theorems proved for the paper's stated cone-based class; no proof of the target scattering-family estimate audited here.
dependencies: Builds on Luk–Oh–Yang cone estimates and Luk–Oh large-data stability results, as specified in the paper.
open_questions: Can the high-order commutations and regular-axis reconstruction be made uniform along the LOY sequence u0→−∞ for compactly supported incoming profiles?
Does any source prove C1 dependence of the selected past-null-infinity scattering solution on its radiation profile?
